text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein meets U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday; discussions cover the peace treaty, economic ties and the situation in Iraq.
- The government denies press reports of an impending move to reduce bread prices and eliminating a current system of cash compensation for Jordanians.
- Results of a poll on the new Majali government show 54.2 percent of Jordanians but only 48.5 percent of opinion makers expect the new government to succeed completely in its responsibilities.
- Crown Prince Hassan says Jordan's relationship with the Palestinians liberates them from Israel.
- King Hussein to discuss with Clinton on Tuesday the Iraqi "case in all its dimensions".
- Finance minister discusses cutting red tape for investors.
- Antiquities minister calls for improving the conditions of work of archaeologists.
- Regent calls on journalists to be accurate and objective.
- Israel and Iraq set to dominate Jordan-U.S. talks.
- Majority of Jordanians believe Majali will be successful as premier -- survey.
